title: The mean of a Poisson distribution
source: S2 Ch2 theory S2-2.1 Quick check 1 (E(X)=3.6 for Po(3.6))
stem: The random variable \(X\) has the distribution \(\mathrm{Po}({l|dp1})\). Write down \(\mathrm{E}(X)\).

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: For a Poisson distribution the mean equals the Poisson parameter.

contexts.stem: If \(X\sim\mathrm{Po}({l|dp1})\), what is the mean of \(X\)?
Write down the mean of a random variable with the distribution \(\mathrm{Po}({l|dp1})\).

stem: A Poisson random variable \(X\) satisfies \(\mathrm{P}(X=1)={l|dp1}\,\mathrm{P}(X=0)\). What is the Poisson parameter?

steps.name: form
steps.note: Use the Poisson formula for r=0 and r=1.

contexts.stem: Given that \(\mathrm{P}(X=1)={l|dp1}\,\mathrm{P}(X=0)\) for a Poisson random variable \(X\), find \(\lambda\).

title: 9709/72/M/J/11 Q3(i): two conditions for a Poisson model

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF, part (i) only, including the opening sentence that introduces X. Parts (ii) and (iii) (Poisson probabilities, including a 10-match product) are omitted so that the item stays with the modelling conditions of this subsection and is not mixed with later probability calculations. Fully manual. Official MS: any two of constant average rate, randomness, or independence, in context (B1 B1); 'scored singly' is not accepted in this context.

stem:
The number of goals scored per match by Everly Rovers is represented by the random variable \(X\) which has mean 1.8.

(i) State two conditions for \(X\) to be modelled by a Poisson distribution.

steps.name: c1
steps.text_tex: A constant average rate of goals scored, or goals occur at random, or goals occur independently (any two, in context).
steps.note: Official MS: any two given in context (B1). Special rule: B1 only if two conditions are given but not in context. 'Goals scored singly' is not accepted here.

steps.name: c2
steps.text_tex: A second distinct condition from the same list, in context.
